paths.description: Homepage and primary video-discovery listing; represents the global shell, navigation, consent, and listing template.
Category index; represents the taxonomy/listing archetype and a high-volume navigation surface.
Representative video detail reached from the homepage; represents the primary watch journey and media-detail template.
Public sign-up surface; represents account creation, input assistance, consent, and authentication choices.
Unknown-route request used to inspect HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not suppress continuous animation
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still reported eight running animations, each with a 2000 ms duration and unbounded iterations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule that removes non-essential animation and auto-advance, retaining only necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Important text has insufficient contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 13 contrast failures, including the age-verification banner at 2.15:1 and supporting text at 1.75:1, both below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe design tokens and test the consent and age-verification surfaces in normal, prefers-contrast, and forced-colors conditions.

findings.summary: Route changes have no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules or declarations, while navigation is through ordinary cross-document links across the primary listing, category, and detail journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin route changes with @view-transition and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long listing chrome does not respond to scroll position
findings.evidence: The homepage screenshot and 4,528 px content layout show a fixed, dense header/sidebar shell; CSS inspection found no scroll-state or scroll-progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent chrome after scroll and provide a lightweight progress or return affordance on long listings.

findings.summary: Consent modal obscures the primary content on every sampled entry path
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots of the homepage, categories, detail, and signup routes show the same large modal covering most of the first viewport before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface that preserves equal accept/reject choices without covering the page purpose and primary action.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is not exposed as a semantic dialog
findings.evidence: DOM probes found zero dialog elements and no role=dialog entry despite the visually modal, page-blocking consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking flow with <dialog>, an accessible name, focus containment/restoration, and an explicit close/decision model.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome competes heavily with content
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains a top navigation row, age banner, sale banner, persistent 190 px sidebar, promotional buttons, and the blocking consent modal, leaving limited room for the content grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate promotions, remove redundant bars, and prioritise the content title and grid in the first viewport.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is rendered at 1,038 px inside a 360 px viewport
findings.evidence: Layout evidence on both homepage and video detail reported scrollWidth/innerWidth 1,038 px against a 360 px visual viewport, producing 678 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the actual mobile layout at the visual viewport width; remove fixed desktop minimum widths and verify at 320–412 px without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not use container-level adaptation
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found zero container rules, and the global desktop shell remained 1,038 px wide at a 360 px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reused cards, navigation, and promo modules containment and adapt them with @container based on available inline size.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible on core controls and some targets are too small
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus showed outline-style none and zero-width outlines on search, login, and promotion buttons. Lighthouse also found target-size failures, and the probe found many 16–20 px interactive targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styles and enlarge or space interactive targets to at least 24 CSS px, preferably 44 px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a raw server error with no recovery path
findings.evidence: The unknown-route test displayed a bare “503 Service Temporarily Unavailable” nginx page with no site navigation, retry, search, or link home.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an intentional branded 404/5xx state with search, home navigation, retry guidance, and correct HTTP status semantics.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is outside the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8 s, FCP 2.9 s, and Speed Index 4.8 s; the root document alone took 1.76 s in that run.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce document latency, prioritise the LCP candidate, and defer non-critical UI and third-party work until after primary content.

findings.summary: The critical path includes a slow document and multiple parser-discovered styles
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 143 requests and 1.86 MB transferred, with three VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheet candidates; Lighthouse measured 1.76 s document response time.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten server response time, inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, and audit each parser-loaded script/style against first-view needs.

findings.summary: The first load ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 57 KiB unused CSS, with 87–95% waste in two mobile stylesheets, plus 26 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR shows 61 script requests and about 1.0 MB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route/component CSS and JavaScript, load consent/auth/media modules on demand, and remove duplicate or unused rules from the initial bundle.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and list structure have accessibility-tree failures
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed buttons, two unnamed links, nine label/name mismatches, and a UL containing disallowed direct children; accessibility score was 0.72.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a discernible name, keep visible labels within accessible names, and restore valid list/landmark semantics.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and semantic reading order are unreliable
findings.evidence: Core buttons had no visible outline when focused, and Lighthouse found invalid list children and inappropriate role=button on a list item containing links.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native interactive elements, valid list children, a logical tab order, and a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and narrow-screen reflow fails
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports user-scalable=no in the effective viewport meta and target-size failures; direct 360 px layout evidence shows 678 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive scale limits, then fix reflow and touch target sizing at mobile and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Localized variants lack explicit hreflang and sitemap discovery signals
findings.evidence: The Malay page links to more than 40 language hosts, but the DOM had no hreflang links; /sitemap.xml returned 404. The canonical also points from xhsocial.com to xhamster.com, so explicit alternate signals are especially important.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish reciprocal hreflang/x-default links for localized equivalents, expose sitemap indexes, and verify canonical host mapping is intentional and consistent.

findings.summary: Content and organization pages expose no rich/share metadata
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph metadata despite representing a media catalog with shareable video-detail entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and VideoObject JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible content on each archetype.

findings.summary: Cookies and security headers are not consistently hardened
findings.evidence: Cookie evidence found three cookies without Secure, including settings and x_csrf_token; settings also uses SameSite=None. Headers omit X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, minimise SameSite=None, protect state tokens appropriately, and add nosniff plus a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: Third-party and analytics traffic begins before the user makes a consent choice
findings.evidence: The initial HAR, captured while the consent modal was still present, recorded 117 third-party-host requests and 1.67 MB transferred, including Google, ad/media hosts, and collector.xhsocial.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics, advertising, recommendation, and identity requests until consent; reduce origins and document each remaining processor.

findings.summary: Public authentication choices omit phishing-resistant sign-in
findings.evidence: The signup surface exposed email/password, Google, and X choices; no passkey/WebAuthn action was present in the inspected public account flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and sign-in as a first-class option, retaining recovery and federation fallbacks.

findings.summary: The Content Security Policy protects only framing
findings.evidence: The CSP is only frame-ancestors self; headers also lack nosniff and Referrer-Policy, while Permissions-Policy allows high-entropy UA model/platform-version hints.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforceable nonce/hash-based CSP, add nosniff and strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and narrow Permissions-Policy to capabilities actually required.

findings.summary: The most important overlay relies on custom runtime semantics
findings.evidence: The blocking consent surface has no dialog/popover primitive, making focus, escape, and restoration behavior dependent on custom JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the flow to <dialog> with explicit focus management and test it at edges, zoom, keyboard-only, and script-failure conditions.

findings.summary: Server failures fall through to an unhelpful nginx page
findings.evidence: The representative invalid route produced a raw 503 response with no retry, navigation, or preserved application context.
findings.suggestedFix: Route 404/5xx failures through a resilient application shell and provide retry, home, and search actions.

findings.summary: The Malay locale is mixed with United Kingdom targeting
findings.evidence: The my.xhsocial.com Malay page displays “GB”, “Kategori Terkenal di UK”, and United Kingdom legal text; network recommendation parameters also use locationCountry=gb and clientLanguage=en.
findings.suggestedFix: Derive language, territory, legal copy, and recommendation locale independently and consistently; do not map Malay language to UK territory defaults.

findings.summary: Consent copy and pre-consent behavior are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The modal says Reject prevents additional cookie purposes, yet the initial load before any choice contacted collector, identity, advertising, and recommendation hosts across 117 third-party-host requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the default state genuinely non-essential-data-free and describe each purpose and partner in language matching observed network behavior.

findings.summary: The email sign-up fields lack native constraint semantics and labels
findings.evidence: After opening email signup, both email and password controls reported required=false; the visible email and password inputs had no associated label, and email used type=text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email, associated labels, required, minlength where appropriate, and interaction-timed accessible validation with aria-invalid/error references.

findings.summary: Email signup disables useful autofill semantics
findings.evidence: The public email field is type=text with autocomplete=off; the password uses new-password correctly, but the email control does not expose email autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email and autocomplete=email for registration while retaining autocomplete=new-password for password creation.

findings.summary: Many images lack dimensions or are oversized
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29 of 36 images without width/height, 14 oversized images, eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 14 legacy-format assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic dimensions, serve right-sized AVIF/WebP candidates with srcset/sizes, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the initial transfer
findings.evidence: HAR attribution assigns 1.67 MB of 1.86 MB and 117 of 143 requests to non-page origins; scripts account for about 1.0 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-specific third-party budgets, defer identity/ads/media until needed or consented, and remove integrations that do not improve the core task.

taskList.title: Rebuild mobile reflow, zoom, focus, and target sizing
Make consent honest, non-blocking, semantic, and pre-consent private
Repair names, roles, list semantics, contrast, and focus
Harden cookies, CSP, and browser security policies
Improve LCP and remove unused initial CSS/JavaScript
Fix locale/territory mapping and localized indexing signals
Optimise image delivery and enforce third-party budgets
Add native, autofill-friendly signup constraints and passkeys
Reduce promotional chrome and respect motion preference
Add structured/share metadata and route transitions
